jobs.title: Corporate Strategy Manager
jobs.description:
About Lyra Health
Lyra Health is a leading provider of evidence-based mental health care, serving more than 20 million people globally in partnership with employers and more than 100 million through health plan and partner relationships. The company has delivered more than 15 million sessions of mental health care, published more than 35 peer-reviewed studies, and delivered unmatched outcomes in terms of access, clinical effectiveness, and cost efficiency. Extensive peer-reviewed research confirms Lyra’s transformative care model helps people recover twice as fast and results in a 26% annual reduction in overall healthcare claims costs. Lyra is transforming access to life-changing mental health care through Lyra Empower, the only fully integrated, AI-powered platform combining the highest-quality care and technology solutions. 


About the Role: 
Reporting to the Director of Strategy, the Corporate Strategy Manager will serve as the core quantitative and analytical engine of the Strategy function. This role owns financial and market modeling, competitor tracking, and project-based strategic initiatives across Lyra's business units.



Responsibilities
-
Quantitative Modeling & Unit Economics: Build financial models, P&L forecasts, and unit economics frameworks to guide portfolio investment decisions and evaluate growth opportunities.

-
Competitive Intelligence & Trends: Perform continuous syntheses of market trends, regulatory shifts, and competitor maneuvers, turning raw data into actionable recommendations for product and market entry teams.

-
Strategic Initiative Execution: Manage day-to-day strategic workstreams supporting M&A target evaluation, 'build vs. buy vs. partner' decisions, and cross-vertical strategic priorities.

-
Annual Planning Support: Structure data collection and analytical inputs to power the annual strategic planning cadence.

-
Executive Presentation Build: Translate complex analytical findings into structured, visual PowerPoint narratives for executive presentation.
Qualifications
-
5+ years of experience in management consulting, corporate strategy, healthcare investment banking, or strategy & operations in a high-growth tech/healthtech setting.

-
Exceptional quantitative and financial modeling capabilities (Excel/Google Sheets) with experience structuring complex datasets.

-
Strong narrative development and visual deck-building skills.

-
Healthcare industry exposure (digital health, employer benefits, or health plans) is strongly preferred.

-
Bachelor’s degree required; top-tier management consulting background preferred.

-

About the Role: 
The Sr. Accounting Transformation Lead is responsible for supporting the SVP, Global Controller to advance the maturity, scalability, and effectiveness of the company's accounting operating model. This role will partner closely with the global leadership team to identify, prioritize, plan and execute accounting transformational initiatives that support the company's growth and long-term strategic objectives.
With the Global Controller, this leader will co-develop and drive accounting transformation spanning organizational design, process standardization, technology enablement, public-company readiness. The successful candidate will combine proven experience in accounting and strategy development, change management, operational excellence.  Sr. Accounting Transformation Lead should have exceptional project management skills along with exceptional communication experience and demonstrated success with delivering excellence for stakeholders.

Responsibilities
Accounting Transformation Strategy

-
Assess current-state capabilities across people, processes, technology, data, governance, and controls and identify opportunities to strengthen the accounting operating model.

-
Translate strategic priorities into project plans with measurable objectives, milestones, dependencies, resource requirements, and expected business outcomes.

Process Excellence & Global Standardization

-
Identify opportunities to simplify, harmonize, automate, and strengthen core accounting processes, including record-to-report, financial close, reconciliations, consolidation, intercompany accounting, financial reporting, and other controllership activities.

-
Manage the development of clearly defined roles, responsibilities, policies, procedures, and performance expectations.

-
Partner with accounting leaders to reduce manual processes, eliminate unnecessary complexity, improve close efficiency, and strengthen the quality and timeliness of financial information.

Technology Automation

-
Identify opportunities to leverage automation, analytics, artificial intelligence, workflow solutions to improve efficiency, accuracy, controls, and decision-making.

-
Partner with Technology and business stakeholders to define requirements, prioritize investments, and ensure successful design and implementation of finance technology solutions.

-
Promote simplification and standardization of systems and data while reducing reliance on fragmented tools and manual processes.

Public Company Readiness

-
Project manage the critical accounting readiness activities associated with SEC-compliant financial reporting, disclosure processes, close and reporting timelines, supporting documentation, and reporting governance.

-
Identify and assist in resolving gaps that could impact IPO timing or sustainable public-company operations.

Change Leadership

-
Provide clear, concise reporting to senior leadership regarding transformation priorities, progress, risks, decisions, and resource requirements.

-
Lead change-management efforts necessary to drive adoption of new processes, technologies, organizational structures, and ways of working.

-
Build strong relationships across functions and geographies and influence stakeholders at all levels of the organization.

-
Promote continuous improvement, accountability, collaboration, and operational excellence across the global Accounting organization.
Qualifications
-
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or related field; CPA strongly preferred.

-
Approximately 12+ years of progressive experience in accounting, controllership, finance transformation, with significant leadership experience in complex, high-growth organizations.

-
Experience leading large-scale Finance or Accounting transformation initiatives involving multiple functions, geographies, systems, and stakeholders.

-
Demonstrated experience redesigning and standardizing accounting processes and operating models.

-
Strong understanding of finance technology ecosystems, including ERP, consolidation, financial reporting, close management, reconciliation, workflow, automation, and data/analytics solutions.

-
Prior experience in public accounting and/or a large, complex multinational organization is a plus.

About the Role:
We are seeking a strategic and experienced Payer Partnership Director to lead the contracting strategy and execution for our Health Plans & Health Systems (HP/HS) vertical. In this role, you will partner closely with business development and the solutions team to drive our market strategy, forge net-new relationships, and ensure optimal payer coverage to support our growth and expand access to care across each market. 
We are looking for someone familiar with cutting-edge approaches to payer contracting in behavioral health at the regional and national level—moving beyond traditional fee-for-service models to champion bundled rates and innovative programs. You will approach these partnerships by offering a value add: directly addressing specialty network gaps and designing tailored products that perfectly match the needs of our payer partners. 

Responsibilities
Payer Contracting Strategy & Execution:

- Lead the end-to-end payer contracting strategy to secure net-new contracts and expand payer coverage in key target markets.

- Negotiate rates, terms, and contract language with national and regional health plans, ensuring agreements are financially viable, sustainable, and aligned with Lyra’s broader business goals.

- Drive the execution of the contracting roadmap from initial outreach to contract execution and implementation.

Market Activation & Cross-Functional Alignment:

- Partner closely with Operations, Business Development, and Clinical leadership to intimately understand the market activation strategy and prioritize contracting targets accordingly.

- Translate market expansion and business development goals into actionable, targeted network development initiatives to ensure robust coverage for prospective and existing clients.

- Serve as a subject matter expert on the payer landscape for internal cross-functional teams, driving alignment on shared goals.

Relationship Development & Management:

- Cultivate, build, and manage strong, long-term relationships with key decision-makers and network managers at national and regional health plans.

- Act as the primary relationship owner for payer partners, navigating complex organizational structures to establish Lyra as a preferred behavioral health partner.

Market Intelligence & Strategic Initiatives:

- Analyze market trends, competitive intelligence, and reimbursement landscapes to continuously refine and inform Lyra’s contracting playbook.

- Track and report on contracting KPIs and network adequacy, nimbly adjusting and reprioritizing strategies to optimize access to care for our members.
Qualifications
- Experience: 12+ years of progressive experience in payer contracting, network development, or managed care, preferably within the digital health, behavioral health, or health tech space.

- Negotiation Expertise: Proven track record of successfully sourcing, negotiating, and executing complex fee-for-service and/or value-based contracts with national and regional health plans.

- Cross-Functional Leadership: Significant experience driving alignment across business development, operations, and executive teams to push toward a shared market strategy.

- Industry Knowledge: Deep understanding of the health plan landscape, credentialing processes, reimbursement methodologies, and regulatory requirements.

- Agility & Drive: A self-starter who thrives in fast-paced, ambiguous environments, with a proven ability to independently build net-new relationships and navigate long, complex sales/contracting cycles.

 As an individual contributor, you will play a key role in administering Lyra’s variable compensation program. You will work closely with cross-functional partners in Finance, Accounting, GTM Operations, Analytics, HR, and other teams to ensure scalable and accurate GTM compensation systems and processes.
This role will administer incentive plans, inquiry management, system development and effectiveness reporting.
 

Responsibilities
-
Commission Operations and Payouts: Calculate monthly, quarterly, and annual incentive payouts for the sales and CS teams with 100% accuracy. Audit underlying booking data, resolve disputes, and ensure payouts align strictly with signed compensation plans and payroll deadlines.

-
CaptivateIQ System Ownership: Serve as the primary administrator and subject matter expert for CaptivateIQ. Manage data integrations (Salesforce, Workday), build and test complex payout logic, maintain compensation models, and optimize the platform for scale.

-
Data Integrity: Own the accuracy of core sales data feeding variable incentive models by auditing customer records, pricing details, and opportunity data in close partnership with Sales, Sales Operations, and Pricing.

-
Reporting & Analytics: Develop and maintain commission reporting dashboards for leadership and finance. Provide actionable insights on incentive effectiveness, attainment trends, and commission costs.

-
Plan Design & Advisory: Partner with leadership, Ops, and HR during annual compensation planning. Model proposed plan structures, evaluate theoretical commission scenarios, and translate compensation plans into operational logic within CaptivateIQ.

-
Audits: Oversee the recurring audit of commission statements before the release of payments, ensuring data integrity and accuracy of plan calculation. Ensure compensation processes are designed to meet audit requirements and that any calculations are fully traceable.

-
Process Optimization: Drive continuous improvement across compensation workflows by identifying process gaps and executing targeted improvements.

-
Field Support: Act as the trusted advisor to the sales organization regarding commission policies. Manage communications with payees related to statements, ensuring clarity and timely responses to any inquiries or discrepancies.
Qualifications
-
8+ years of experience in variable compensation and sales/revenue operations.

-
Bachelor's Degree in Business Administration, Finance, HR, or a related field.

-
Proven experience in designing, implementing, and managing sales variable compensation programs, preferably within a high-growth go-to-market team.

-
Analytical skills with the ability to interpret complex sales data, determine trends, and draw valid conclusions.

-
Knowledge of relevant compliance and legal requirements about sales compensation.

-
3+ years of hands-on experience administering Incentive Compensation Management (ICM) platforms, with CaptivateIQ experience strongly preferred.

-
Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and meet deadlines.

-
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to work effectively with a diverse group of stakeholders, including senior leadership.

-
Ability to problem-solve and make informed decisions, especially in high-pressure situations.

-
An understanding of the broader go-to-market strategy and how compensation drives sales behavior.
